Promoters, coding regions, and intron-exon boundaries of LCAT (NM_012108.3) were amplified by polymerase chain reaction and purified by ExoSap-IT (USB).

cases.statement: Two siblings (brother and sister), both homozygous for c.605T>C p.(Ile202Thr). Both have very low HDL cholesterol, corneal opacity and nearly absent LCAT activity; only the brother developed renal disease.

people.label: first case (first patient)
people.key_phenotypes: extremely low HDL cholesterol; corneal opacities; proteinuria since mid-forties; progressive renal disease requiring hemodialysis at 75; nearly absent cholesterol esterification

quotes.quote: The first patient was referred to our Lipid Unit for an extremely low plasma concentration of HDL cholesterol, corneal opacities and progressive renal disease when he was 65 years old.
He reported low plasma levels of total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, moderately elevated TG and proteinuria since his mid-forties.
He developed progressive renal disease requiring hemodialysis at the age of 75 and he died 12 years later.
| HDL cholesterol mg/dL | 7 | 14 | 13 | 40–60 |
Genetic analysis of both siblings revealed a homozygous mutation c.605T>C, which is predicted to cause a substitution of isoleucine by threonine at amino acid 202 of LCAT, p.(Ile202Thr).

people.label: second case (second patient, sister of the first)
people.key_phenotypes: extremely low HDL cholesterol; corneal opacity for 30 years; no renal disease and no proteinuria at 84

quotes.quote: The second patient, sister of the first patient, was a 78-year-old female, that was also referred to our Lipid Unit for an extremely low plasma concentration of HDL cholesterol in a routine analysis.
This patient reported that she had suffered from corneal opacity during the last 30 years.
Currently, she is 84 years old, asymptomatic, and her renal function remains within normal values, including urinalysis without proteinuria.
Genetic analysis of both siblings revealed a homozygous mutation c.605T>C, which is predicted to cause a substitution of isoleucine by threonine at amino acid 202 of LCAT, p.(Ile202Thr).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Both siblings show very low HDL cholesterol, corneal opacity and nearly absent endogenous LCAT activity; the brother also had proteinuria and progressive renal disease. The authors note the brother had no diabetes or hypertension that could explain the nephropathy. No testing of other genes is reported.

quotes.quote: The cholesterol esterification rate in serum, as a measure of endogenous LCAT activity, in all cases, was nearly absent, as compared with control values (1.70 nmol/h*mL, 0.05 nmol/h*mL and 1.35 nmol/h*mL, respectively).

The first case reported developed renal disease, and, although this could have been caused by other diseases, the patient demonstrated progressive proteinuria, without other pathologies, such as diabetes or hypertension, which could have conditioned the development of nephropathy.

segregation.statement: Two affected siblings are both homozygous. The authors say genetic analysis was extended to all available family members (Figure S1), but the text gives no genotypes or counts for other relatives. The authors' group previously reported the variant in heterozygous people with hypoalphalipoproteinemia.

quotes.quote: The genetic analysis was extended to all available family members of the siblings (Figure S1).
The first mutation, p.(Ile202Thr), has been previously associated with hypoalphalipoproteinemia in the heterozygosity state by our group [22] (Table 1).

in_trans.statement: Homozygous in both siblings. Parental testing and consanguinity are not reported.

quotes.quote: Genetic analysis of both siblings revealed a homozygous mutation c.605T>C, which is predicted to cause a substitution of isoleucine by threonine at amino acid 202 of LCAT, p.(Ile202Thr).

functional.statement: Patient plasma only (no construct). Exogenous LCAT activity (reassembled HDL substrate) and endogenous activity (FER) were far below reference in both siblings. Table 1 and the Results text assign the exogenous values (0.05 and 1.7 nmol/h*mL) and FER values (1.50 and 1.40 %/h) to the two siblings in opposite order.

quotes.quote: Plasma LCAT activity was determined using reassembled HDL, containing 1-palmitoyl-2-oleyl-sn-3-phosphocholine, [^3H] cholesterol, and apo A-I.
| Exogenous LCAT activity (nmol/h*mL) | 0.05 | 1.7 | 1.35 | (23.0–57.0) |
| Endogenous LCAT activity (Fractional esterification rate, %/h) | 1.50 | 1.40 | 1.90 | >3.50% |
All patients reported null endogenous LCAT activity, with an FER of 1.40%, 1.5% and 1.9% per hour, respectively, below the minimum reference value (value reference: >3.5% by hour) (Table 1).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense as stated in the paper (p.(Ile202Thr)); the batch's predicted protein from the stated accession is p.(Leu202Pro) (see concerns). The authors place the residue near the subdomain close to the catalytic site and describe FLD as absent or catalytically inactive enzyme.

quotes.quote: The mutation p.(Ile202Thr) is located close to the second subdomain, formed by the insertions between β6/β7 and β7/αE, which is in much closer proximity to the catalytic site [23,24].
In FLD, the LCAT enzyme is either absent in plasma, or exhibits no catalytic activity on any lipoprotein [6].

computational_predictions.statement: The authors report a summary prediction from PolyPhen-2, MutationTaster and PredictSNP (wording quoted); no scores given.

quotes.quote: Both mutations have been classified as pathogenic by bioinformatic analysis (Polyphen-2 [19], MutationTaster [20] and Predict SNP [21]).

authors_classification.statement: The authors state the variant was classified as pathogenic by bioinformatic analysis (in-silico only), and that it had not previously been described in LCAT-deficient patients.

quotes.quote: Both mutations have been classified as pathogenic by bioinformatic analysis (Polyphen-2 [19], MutationTaster [20] and Predict SNP [21]).
In the present study, we report three cases with FLD with corneal opacities, due to two homozygous mutations (c.605T>C, c.512G>A) not previously described in patients with LCAT deficiency.

concerns: MAPPING PROBLEM: the batch's hgvs_c uses the accession the paper states (NM_012108.3), and the resulting vcf_grch38 lies on chromosome 4, whereas the paper places LCAT on chromosome 16q21-22 ('encoded by a gene located on chromosome 16q21-22'). The predicted protein from that accession (Leu202Pro) differs from the paper's p.(Ile202Thr) (protein_check: differs). The stated accession may not be an LCAT transcript; the panel should re-map c.605T>C / p.(Ile202Thr) on the LCAT reference transcript before assessing this candidate, and its gap status should be re-checked after re-mapping.

The paper contradicts itself on which sibling has which activity value: Table 1 gives exogenous 0.05 (first case) and 1.7 (second case) nmol/h*mL and FER 1.50 / 1.40 %/h, while the Results text lists 1.70, 0.05 and 1.35 nmol/h*mL and FER 1.40%, 1.5% and 1.9% 'respectively'.
Results say the first patient 'died 12 years later' after hemodialysis at 75, while Table 1 lists his current age as 88.
Family testing was extended to relatives (Figure S1) but the genotypes of relatives are not given in the text.
Clinical discordance within the sibship (renal disease only in the brother) is discussed by the authors as due to factors other than genotype.
notes_for_panel: Strong biochemical phenotype in two homozygous siblings, but the candidate's genomic coordinate and predicted protein come from an accession that does not appear to match LCAT. Resolve the mapping first: if the paper's c.605T>C refers to LCAT codon Ile202, the coordinate in this candidate is wrong.
